findings.text: style profile declares motion_ceiling=3 (more motion than the ceiling-1 baseline) but the render's KEN_BURNS_SCALE constant is still 1.03 (the restrained value calibrated for motion_ceiling=1) - stills will look flatter/more static than this style profile intends
findings.reasoning: Cross-checked motion_ceiling's actual documented usage (bible/Module_06 §Flow production, Module_15, Module_19) - in every reference it governs the CAMERA MOTION INTENSITY OF FLOW-GENERATED VIDEO SHOTS ('no shot exceeds the template's motion_ceiling', 'respect the template's camera_vocabulary and motion_ceiling'), not the Ken-Burns pan/zoom Remotion applies to STILL images in post. This project's 3 real AI-video shots (SH-003-01/006-01/008-01) already carry whatever motion Flow generated into the baked footage - motion_ceiling: 3 was satisfied at generation time, not at render time. slideshow_risk.py's motion_ceiling_findings check is a useful heuristic pairing (documented in its own source comment as calibrated 'for most style profiles' where ceiling happens to be 1) but is not a hard rule that every style's ceiling value must scale the Remotion Ken-Burns constant proportionally - no other completed project in this studio has done so. KEN_BURNS_SCALE=1.03 is the calibrated documentary-restrained baseline used successfully across 5 completed projects; bumping it for stills specifically was not requested and has no evidence behind it for this project. Not silently skipped (CLAUDE.md law #4) - reviewed and documented here before the full render.
